items.observation: Operational guide has method routing and error extrema, but should substantiate when exact COUNT is faster than sampling and when conditional sampling wins, without suggesting approximate smallness authorizes production scans.
items.requiredResolution: Use a SMALL immutable empirical comparison from the105 static frontier (e.g.250k dense COUNT versus3% sample,3M wide COUNT versus3/10% sample), plus existing-index/default COUNT plan guidance on the isolated acquisition target. Verify numeric fields and measured interval differences. Do not imply a universal fastest algorithm, controlled cache parity, a row-count-only safety threshold, or create a new index on primary just to count. State exact default COUNT with suitable existing index may beat sampling; precision-required sampling must meet all acceptance conditions. No new experiment grid.

items.observation: Historical extrema/cost figures remain valid only within their stated observation sets. The new narrowed run may show worse error, lower precision completion or different ordering.
items.requiredResolution: Inspect fresh metadata93, encrypted91,105static and48service outcomes. Do not cherry-pick favorable historical values or ignore a fresh counterexample. Add important new extrema/limitations with their immutable new snapshot and precise conditions, keeping old and new sets distinct. Never infer global guarantees or causal rankings from either.

items.observation: Initial TABLES SQL can retrieve engine statistics when cache is absent/expired or existing stats_expiry is0. Reading the expiry setting without a decision branch is not a cache-only safety gate. Even metadata is not guaranteed zero additional production impact.
items.requiredResolution: Make the first safe action check existing approved inventory/monitoring stats and acquisition budget/target before issuing SQL. Explain cached stats miss/expiry fallback and already0 settings; do not blindly run the full SQL block on primary. If no extra primary impact is acceptable or budget/monitoring is unavailable, use existing exported stats/isolated acquisition or defer. Keep UNKNOWN and freshness explicit. Do not imply a nonzero expiry forces cache-only reads or silently escalate mysql-schema privileges. Use a NEW dedicated connection even for the initial stats SQL; setting autocommit=1 on an existing application transaction can commit unrelated work. Do not reuse pooled application sessions or change global settings. For cancellation identify the currently owned query using job identity/tag, target/account and start context, not stale CONNECTION_ID alone; do not blindly KILL a recycled ID. If ownership/cancellation cannot be verified, require the owner path before starting the exact job. Monitor recovery after query termination until service metrics return within the owner budget; cache/IO impact can outlast the COUNT. No immediate blind retry after cancellation.

items.observation: First narrowed white-all process passed but owner rejected performance-window semantics because wall-clock endpoints regressed; immutable snapshot review-20261107T142407Z-3330 and owner-essential-semantic-rejection preserve failure. items.requiredResolution: Keep the rejected observation distinct from valid query durations/counts/accuracy and the fresh monotonic run. Do not reuse affected/unknown-clock service windows as SLO or causal performance evidence. Integrate only actual new proof/source/cleanup audits; describe historical limitations briefly in evidence routing, not as a burden on guideline users.
